                  </ns0:note> And while they abode in Galilee, Jesus said unto them, The son of man shall be betrayed into the hands of men.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 And they shall kill him, and the third day he shall be raised again, And they were exceeding sorry.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 9.30, 31, 32. <ns0:hi>And they departed thence, and passed through Galilee, and he would not that any Man should know it. For he taught his Disciples, and said unto them, the Son of Man is delivered into the Hands of Men, and they shall kill him, and after that he is killed, he shall rise the third Day. But they understood not that Saying, and were afraid to ask him. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 9.44. he said unto them, <ns0:hi>Let these Sayings sink down into your Ears; for the Son of Man shall be delivered into the hands of Men. But they understood not this Saying, and it was hid from them; that they perceived it not, and they feared to ask him that saying</ns0:hi>: It is said, That Christ taught his Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples, as they were able to hear, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 4.33.9. he tells them <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 16.12. <ns0:hi>He had many things to say unto them, but they could not hear them at that time.</ns0:hi> Christ a long time con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cealed the Doctrine of his <ns0:hi>Passion,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Resurrection</ns0:hi> from the dead, from them, until he had confirmed them in the great point of his <ns0:hi>Divine Power,</ns0:hi> and his being the true <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>; now he begins to deliver this Doctrine unto them, that what they should now soon see, might not weaken their Faith in him, as the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> and the Son of God: Partly, in regard of that inveterate Opinion, which had possessed the Generality of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> that the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> should be a temporal Prince, and should deliver the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> from that Servitude, under which they were, and had for a long time been: Partly, in regard of the Difficulty to conceive, how he who was the Son of God could dye. Once or twice before therefore he had begun to speak to them, about his Passion, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 16.21. <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> had some Discourse with him about it, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 9.31. The Text saith, <ns0:hi>They understood it not,</ns0:hi> It <ns0:hi>was hid from them. They perceived it not. They were afraid to ask him. They were Sorry.</ns0:hi> Possibly they were sorry, that they could not understand it, and reconcile it to the Notion of the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> they had drank in, for it seems hard to assert, they were sorry for what Christ said about his suffering, because the Scripture saith, <ns0:hi>they understood it not,</ns0:hi> thinking our Saviour had not spoken plain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly of a matter of Fact which should be, but that he intended something else, besides what his Words seemed plainly to im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />port.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>

That take, and give unto them for me and thee.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Jews were by Gods Law, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 30.13. obliged to pay an <ns0:hi>half Shekel,</ns0:hi> which was for the <ns0:hi>Service of</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Sanctuary, v.</ns0:hi> 16. this was paid every year, the half Shekel amounted in our Money to fifteen Pence, or there abouts, whether this were the Tribute Money here demanded, and paid, some doubt, and say that the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> having the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> now under their Power, imposed this payment upon every Head, as a Tribute to the <ns0:hi>Emperor,</ns0:hi> which being a <ns0:hi>Cu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stomary payment,</ns0:hi> they thought the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> would less <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>umble at, tho it was changed from a <ns0:hi>Sacred,</ns0:hi> to a <ns0:hi>Civil use,</ns0:hi> from an Homage Peny to God, to be an Homage Peny to the <ns0:hi>Conquerors.</ns0:hi> The Agreement of this Sum, with what was required by the Law, together with what our Saviour saith af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terward, will incline us to think, that this Tax was that <ns0:hi>Re<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>i<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gious Tax</ns0:hi> mentioned, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 30. and that the <ns0:hi>Collectors</ns0:hi> were some <ns0:hi>Officers</ns0:hi> deputed for that Service by the <ns0:hi>Priests.</ns0:hi> When <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> came into the house, our Saviour preventeth his pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pounding the <ns0:hi>Question</ns0:hi> to him (for <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> had before told them, <ns0:hi>yes he did</ns0:hi>) by asking him of whom the <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Earth</ns0:hi> use to <ns0:hi>receive Tribute,</ns0:hi> of their own <ns0:hi>Children</ns0:hi> or of <ns0:hi>Strangers</ns0:hi>? where by <ns0:hi>Children,</ns0:hi> we must not understand their <ns0:hi>Political Children,</ns0:hi> that is their <ns0:hi>Subjects,</ns0:hi> but their <ns0:hi>Natural Children</ns0:hi> for otherwise <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> would not have said of <ns0:hi>Stran<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gers,</ns0:hi> nor would our Saviour have Answered, <ns0:hi>Then are the Children free,</ns0:hi> for there is nothing more ordinary than for <ns0:hi>Princes</ns0:hi> to receive <ns0:hi>Tribute</ns0:hi> of their <ns0:hi>Subjects.</ns0:hi> That which our Saviour seemeth to mean is this, This Tribute is gathered for my Heavenly Father. I am his Son, I am not bound to pay it. <ns0:hi>Notwithstanding lest we offend,</ns0:hi> Lest we give them oc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />casion to say we break the Law of God, Go thou to the Sea, (the Sea of <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi> which was near) and <ns0:hi>take up the Fish, which cometh up first, and when thou hast opened his Mouth, thou shalt find</ns0:hi>

                     </ns0:gap> a piece of Money, to the value of a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bout an half Crown in <ns0:hi>English.</ns0:hi> How this Money came in the Mouth of the Fish, is a very idle dispute, considering that he that speakes, was the Creator of all things. And <ns0:hi>pay thou for me and thee.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> who think they have found here an Argument for the <ns0:hi>Primacy</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> because Christ paid this Tribute for him, and not for the other Disciples, do not only affirm what they do not know, but forget that <ns0:hi>Capernaum</ns0:hi> was the City in which <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> lived, (we heard be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore of Christs curing his Wives Mother there of a Feaver) and that <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> was the only Man of whom this Tribute was de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manded. This Portion of Scripture affords us this Instructi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on. <ns0:hi>That it is the Duty of Christians, to yield some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing of their own right, when they cannot insist upon, and obtain it without a Scandal, and prejudice to the Gospel, and the concern of Religion.</ns0:hi> If this were required in pursuance of the Law, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 30.12, 13. and our Saviour had refused to pay it, the Scribes, and <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> would have Clamoured against him, as Violating the Law of God. If it were re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quired as a Civil Tax, they would have Clamoured against him, as a Man that went about to stir up <ns0:hi>Sedition,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Rebel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lion.</ns0:hi> Having therefore first asserted his right, and immuni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty, he departeth from it, to prevent a Scandal. We must never part with Gods right: but to depart from our own, is not only lawful, but oftentimes very advisable, and expedient. Our Saviour chuseth rather to Work a <ns0:hi>Miracle,</ns0:hi> than to give a <ns0:hi>Scandal,</ns0:hi> and by this <ns0:hi>Miracle</ns0:hi> he also confirmed his Im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />munity, that he was the Son of him, who is the <ns0:hi>King of Kings,</ns0:hi> and so not in strictness obliged to pay it.</ns0:note>
